For any candidate linear space V, derivative at zero is an injective linear map into a nonsingular real matrix subspace, bounded by the proved Adams--Lax--Phillips theorem. Hurwitz--Radon skew orthogonal anticommuting matrices provide rho(n)-dimensional spaces W containing identity, all nonzero members invertible. The transfer A -> A composed with any given F is injective and preserves collisions and nonzero constant Jacobians, giving pointwise matching lower bound. The standalone checker confirms the sample identities, not the infinite theorem.
